Section 3 Mode 3 specifies checking M + M^T >= 0 via 'exact rational symmetric pivoted congruence elimination' without stating how zero diagonal pivots with nonzero off-diagonal entries (indefinite 2x2 blocks) are handled in the PDF text itself.

summary: This 4-page manuscript presents a two-layer, zero-floating-point verification companion for four discrete-algebraic mechanisms from a companion November 24, 2026 OpenAI preprint [7] on strongly polynomial linear programming: (Layer 1) 18 standalone constructive Lean 4.35.0 scalar integer/natural sub-lemmas without Classical.choice or external imports, and (Layer 2) a pure-int/Fraction Python 4-mode certificate auditor (SPLP-SMALE9-CERT-1.0) evaluated on 16 canonical finite witnesses (0.049-0.485 ms) and 73 adversarial forgeries. All 18 Table 1 theorem statements, all four hand-verifiable worked witnesses (C01, C05, C11, C13), the Section 9.3 Fig. 5 clipped-update trajectory, and cross-references among text, tables, and figures are internally consistent and mathematically exact as printed. While the Lean 4 layer only formalizes elementary 1D scalar arithmetic proxies (and none of the core algorithmic or strongly polynomial complexity pillars of [7] are verified), the manuscript explicitly and honestly discloses these boundaries.
weaknesses: Mathematical triviality of the Lean 4 kernel: all 18 theorems in Table 1 are 1-to-3-line scalar arithmetic or ring identities over Z or N (e.g., by = cx => by - cx = 0, 2^k - 1 < 2^k, u(a*mu) + mu(-a*u) = 0). No matrices, vectors, rationals, LP duality, general-k Newton identities, or contraction fixed-point theorems are formalized in Lean.

Proxy mismatch in Lean scalarizations: sec72_monotone_lcp_gap_split and sec73_qp_skew_block_monotone reduce d-dimensional non-symmetric monotone/skew matrices to 1D scalars where non-symmetry vanishes, and sec31_reciprocal_scaling_preserves_product proves dr = 1 over Z rather than dyadic rationals 2^{+/-p_i}.

Limited scope and empirical scale of Layer 2: the substantive mathematical checks (matrix rank, orthogonal complements, Newton determinants for k <= 5, PSD congruence for d <= 5, clipped Bellman updates for n <= 4) reside in an unverified Python script tested on only 16 small handcrafted certificates.

Title/abstract framing ('Constructive Lean 4 Kernel ... for OpenAI's Strongly Polynomial Linear Programming' and 'algebraic and duality sub-lemmas') slightly overstates what Lean actually proves, even though Proposition 1 and Explicit Non-Claims clarify the scalar scope.
